title: Prefs: Add back support for console.log.level.
description:
If the user supplies a console.log.level option, map it as best we can
to its equivalent ws_log level and write messages to stderr.
Fixes #17763.

notes.body: assigned to @geraldcombs
@jvalverde I tried to add a `ws_log(..., "please use --log-level instead")` message, but couldn't get it to show up.
I don't understand what you mean, sorry.
Mistake on my part. Please disregard.
It's the other way around.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/5380/diffs?diff_id=292821954&start_sha=7ffdbf49f7bc2c8fd227a4783e98eb74d4436fe2#6dda3f5ebb645b0b7da005c76b0f7b0c2b30807a_5864_5864)
I was assuming we'd want the noisiest level to take precedence. Is that not the case?

Sorry, I wasn't clear. I was referring to the comment:

> `// GLib logging wrote to stderr.`

GLib logging writes to stderr levels above info. It writes to stdout levels info and debug. This change does not match the stream output behavior in 3.4, as far as I know, which I presume is one of your goals.

> Ah, OK. The latest patch prints the "up and ready" message using LOG_LEVEL_INFO, which should match the stdio and visibility behavior of previous versions.

Agreed. Looking at the code I think it matches previous versions.

> Shouldn't that be "||" instead of "&&"?

I don't think so. By design only levels Info and below are configurable with `ws_log_console_writer_set_use_stderr()`. The others are not affected.

GLib writes debug and info messages to stdout. wslog was implemented to write to stderr always. This is the correct behavior but because it broke extcap communication with the GUI wslog was changed to imitate GLib. It may change again in the future.

https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/blob/main/glib/gmessages.c#L1181

```c
/**
 * g_log_writer_default_set_use_stderr:
 * @use_stderr: If %TRUE, use `stderr` for log messages that would
 *  normally have appeared on `stdout`
 *
 * Configure whether the built-in log functions
 * (g_log_default_handler() for the old-style API, and both
 * g_log_writer_default() and g_log_writer_standard_streams() for the
 * structured API) will output all log messages to `stderr`.
 *
 * By default, log messages of levels %G_LOG_LEVEL_INFO and
 * %G_LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG are sent to `stdout`, and other log messages are
 * sent to `stderr`. This is problematic for applications that intend
 * to reserve `stdout` for structured output such as JSON or XML.
 *
 * This function sets global state. It is not thread-aware, and should be
 * called at the very start of a program, before creating any other threads
 * or creating objects that could create worker threads of their own.
 *
 * Since: 2.68
 */
```

> This is the correct behavior but because it broke extcap communication with the GUI wslog was changed to imitate GLib. It may change again in the future.

I would rather do the right thing here and write to stderr always, rather than have this complicated logic to switch streams. This interface to select sdterr was an expedient but it just seems like technical debt now.
I think the better way to do what you are trying to do (a compatibility shim) is to hack `ws_log_parse_args()` to recognize `-o console.log.level`.
I will give this a go.
Implemented in !5393.

This option isn't being added to the preferences, but for people coming from other versions it has the usual problems with preferences that disappeared if you remove this.

We currently [exit with an error](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/ui/commandline.c#L524) if you pass in an obsolete preference on the command line. I suppose we could not do that.

commits_data.message:
Prefs: Add back support for console.log.level.

If the user supplies a console.log.level option, map it as best we can
to its equivalent ws_log level. Print Wireshark's "up and ready" message
using LOG_LEVEL_INFO, which goes to stdout to match previous versions.
Fixes #17763.
